chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Al-Barqi from a Sheikh who raised the hadith to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He said to him, 'O So-and-so, reduce the expenditure for Hajj so that you will be eager for Hajj, and do not increase the expenditure in Hajj lest you become weary of Hajj.'
ai.seo_question: How does the amount of money spent on Hajj affect one's spiritual state and eagerness for the pilgrimage?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises minimizing Hajj expenses to preserve spiritual enthusiasm, warning that excessive financial burden can lead to *tamallu* (wearying or resenting) the act of worship. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *suhla* (ease) and the psychological sustainability of religious duties, ensuring the pilgrim remains mentally present and grateful rather than viewing Hajj as a heavy financial strain.
